simple.meaning: דּוֹדָה (dôwdâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “an aunt.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דּוֹדָה (H1733) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 6:20, with occurrences in Exodus, Leviticus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דּוֹדָה (H1733) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דּוֹדָה (H1733) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דּוֹדָה (dôwdâh) / H1733 is traced through Exodus 6:20, Leviticus 18:14, Leviticus 20:20 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses. The years of the life of Amram were one hundred thirty-seven years.

timeline.evidenceText: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses. The years of the life of Amram were one hundred thirty-seven years.
“ ‘You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother. You shall not approach his wife. She is your aunt.
If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They shall bear their sin. They shall die childless.
